destroy()

The destroy() method permanently tears down a FeatureCell instance and releases all resources associated with its runtime execution. Destroy is a lifecycle operation that finalizes the FeatureCell and prevents any further pipeline execution, state updates, or emissions.

Method Contract Summary

  • Terminates the FeatureCell lifecycle
  • Tears down behaviors and controllers
  • Completes internal event streams
  • Prevents further state updates or pipeline execution
  • Invoked automatically when the hosting provider is destroyed

The destroy() method defines finalization and teardown only. It does not perform state computation, emit snapshots, or participate in pipeline execution. Its responsibility is limited to releasing resources and permanently shutting down the FeatureCell runtime surface.

Note

In typical application usage, destroy() is called automatically by the hosting framework or provider lifecycle. Manual invocation is supported but should be reserved for advanced lifecycle control or non-standard hosting environments.

Example

Calling destroy() permanently deactivates the FeatureCell. Once destroyed, the FeatureCell cannot be re-initialized, cannot emit state, and cannot participate in Vault-managed execution.

Example: Destroying a FeatureCell

{{`// Explicitly destroy the FeatureCell
employeeCell.destroy();

// FeatureCell is now permanently torn down`}}

What this does

  • Tears down all registered behaviors
  • Destroys all associated controllers
  • Completes internal event and lifecycle streams
  • Prevents further state updates or pipeline execution

After destruction, any attempt to interact with the FeatureCell runtime surface is invalid and may result in runtime errors or no-op behavior, depending on the hosting environment.
